messages.subject: Warning Error message/read.cross
parts:
Hi
I,m trying to read in data (similiar format as hyper , bc) with AA,
AB, BB and phenotypic data as well

hyper<-read.cross(format="csv", file="D:\\try\
\tryril.csv",genotypes=c("AA","BB"),
na.strings=c("na"),alleles=c("A","B"), convertXdata=TRUE)

but i get these error messages
Warning messages:
1: In read.cross.csv(dir, file, na.strings, genotypes,
estimate.map, :
The following unexpected genotype codes were treated as missing.
|NA|AB|

2: In FUN(X[[3L]], ...) :
The phenotype value "NA" was interpreted as missing.
3: In FUN(X[[3L]], ...) :
The phenotype value "NA" was interpreted as missing.
4: In FUN(X[[3L]], ...) :
The phenotype value "NA" was interpreted as missing.

also when I run scantwo


Warning message:
In checkcovar(cross, pheno.col, addcovar, intcovar, perm.strata, :
Dropping 1 individuals with missing phenotypes.



I get stange LOD scores most of them in zeros or negatives maybe I
need to do something to read in file in bettere way.


Any suggestion?
Cheers

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Warning Error message/read.cross
parts:
In read.cross, use genotypes=c("AA","AB","BB") and na.strings="NA"

However the file name, "tryril.csv", indicates that these are RILs, in which case you should note that R/qtl can't handle heterozygous genotypes in RIL, and must treat them as missing. And so, aside from the "na" vs "NA", what you are doing is correct, but you need to afterwards convert from backcross (which is hopefully how the data are interpreted) to "riself" or "risib", which you can do with the functions convert2riself() or convert2risib(). For example:

hyper <- convert2riself(hyper)

The first warning message in scantwo just says that there was an individual (or line) with missing phenotype, and so that individual was omitted from the analysis.

It's hard to know what the 0's and negative LOD scores mean without seeing the data.

karl
